ranked_evidence.title: Cake freebie request from The Voice 'abysmal', says bakery - BBC
ranked_evidence.snippet: # Cake freebie request from The Voice 'abysmal'. An independent bakery owner has said it was a "kick in the teeth" to be asked by The Voice UK to provide the ITV show's guests and judges with free cakes. Rich Myers, 37, from Get Baked, which has its flagship store in Manchester, described the request as a "total disgrace", adding that large companies should not ask small businesses to supply products in return for so-called "exposure". Myers shared the email on Instagram, which said ITV was unable to pay but the food would be seen by "highly influential" coaches, presenters and contestants. Lifted Entertainment, which makes The Voice UK for ITV, apologised and said "steps had been taken to ensure this type of request is never made again". "ITV and Lifted Entertainment, you're a total disgrace," he wrote on Instagram. "When you're new to it all, you get an email from someone like The Voice and it's got ITV on the signature," he said.

A survivor of the Nova music festival terrorist attack by Hamas pushed back against a video released by Zohran Mamdani calling Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu a "war criminal," saying the New York City mayor’s comments were "dangerous.". Mazal Tazazo made the remark in a video shared on X by radio host Jason Rantz, one day after Mamdani said Netanyahu was "the architect of a horrific genocide against the Palestinian people.". In Mamdani’s message, he said he agreed with the International Criminal Court that "Benjamin Netanyahu should be arrested and tried for his crimes" and urged the federal government to carry out an arrest warrant if Netanyahu visits New York City in September for the U.N. ranked_evidence.snippet: # Machete-wielding man confronted by police at UCI Health in Los Alamitos, prompting lockdown. A medical center in Los Alamitos was placed on lockdown as police confronted a machete-wielding man in a parking lot. (KABC) -- A medical center in Los Alamitos was placed on lockdown Wednesday morning as police confronted a machete-wielding man in a parking lot. The incident occurred at UCI Health - Los Alamitos, resulting in a massive response by officers from at least two agencies. A swarm of officers from the Long Beach and Los Alamitos police departments descended on the medical center located at 3751 Katella Avenue around 11 a.m. A bystander's video showed the shirtless suspect pacing back and forth on a sidewalk, swinging the machete and apparently yelling at nearby officers. The Orange County Sheriff's Department said its deputies were not involved in the response and referred questions to the Long Beach Police Department.

ranked_evidence.title: For Taylor Swift, Madison Square Garden’s Controversial Cameras Briefly Went Dark - WIRED
ranked_evidence.snippet: Madison Square Garden owner James Dolan has insisted that the face-recognition system and array of surveillance cameras deployed at his venues is “very, very useful for security”—a big reason why MSG “is the most secure venue in the country.”. On the night of July 2, security in and around the Garden was particularly intense. July 2 was, of course, the kickoff to Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce’s wedding celebration, an approximately 100-person rehearsal dinner at Madison Square Garden’s Infosys Theater. And yet, on that extremely sensitive evening, Dolan’s MSG locked nearly all of its security team out of the network of surveillance cameras inside the arena, according to an internal document reviewed by WIRED. According to the internal document, an MSG executive ordered on July 2 a seven-hour lockdown of the Garden’s video management system, made by the security tech company Genetec, “due to a client privacy request.” Security staffers who ordinarily monitor the building’s internal cameras and the accompanying face-recognition software were barred from doing so.

ranked_evidence.title: Self-styled journalists test the limits of press freedom - The Kathmandu Post
ranked_evidence.snippet: A growing trend of filming and confronting civil servants on camera for social media clicks is blurring the line between journalism and intimidation. Screengrabs from YouTube videos show self-styled journalists questioning government employees at their workplaces. The videos typically feature surprise inspections in which government employees are questioned about attendance, identity cards and dress codes. Across Nepal, a growing number of self-styled journalists carrying microphones and cameras have been walking into government offices, confronting public officials, filming tense exchanges with employees and posting the footage online in the name of ‘investigative journalism’ or ‘surprise inspections’. Media experts, journalists and government officials say the trend bears little resemblance to journalism and instead amounts to intimidation disguised as public accountability. But the explosion of social media and online content has blurred the boundaries of professional journalism. Jhabindra Bhusal, chief officer at the Press Council Nepal, the regulatory body responsible for enforcing the journalist code of conduct, said that barging into government offices with microphones and intimidating employees is a clear violation of journalistic ethics.
